title: Telemetry batch eraser with immutable audit manifest and safe-delete window
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: implement a resilient, auditable batch eraser for console telemetry and usage metrics that supports a reversible quarantine window and an irreversible safe-delete phase. This ticket delivers: 1) an immutable, append-only audit manifest format for all delete intents (manifest entries contain object keys, query predicates, tombstone IDs, SHA256 checksum, signer metadata, and deletion window timestamps), 2) a two-phase delete operator (quarantine -> safe-delete) with idempotent retries and reconciliation, and 3) glue to S3 lifecycle + KMS + analytics backfill so derived aggregated views can be escrowed or regenerated if needed. This design aims to satisfy compliance requests for provable deletion while avoiding accidental data loss from race conditions with streaming ingestion or billing reports.
acceptance_criteria: Audit manifest records are written to a write-once bucket path and include checksum+signature; manifests are queryable by deletion id and time range.
Two-phase delete operator supports: create-delete-intent -> quarantine (retention window configurable per-customer) -> final-purge; operator is idempotent and survives process restarts.
Deleted objects are recorded in an immutable audit log and linked to an attestation artifact (signed manifest). Attestation artifacts can be exported for legal review.

Backfill job can detect and escrow aggregated views (hourly/day partitions) referenced by delete intent; escrowed artifacts are stored encrypted and tagged for later reconstitution if under legal hold.
No increase in query latency or pipeline SLO violations during standard operation; deletion throughput targets: 10k small object deletes/min at P95 within quotas.
Runbook created with steps to pause deletes, rehydrate escrow, and perform emergency rollback; deletion metrics and dashboards added to Console.
Integration tests and a canary pipeline validated against a staging dataset containing synthetic PII and simulated legal-hold flags.

next_steps: Finalize S3 lifecycle finalized policy (responsible: infra), complete legal-hold rehydrate test (responsible: eng-qa), schedule security sign-off on KMS envelope change, and roll out canary to us-west-2 for 48h. After successful canary, enable gradual rollout by customer cohort (tiered by commit and dedicated customers).
risks: Race with streaming pipeline writes may lead to partial deletes if gating isn't enforced; mitigation: ingestion-side check and backfill reconciliation job.
Compliance teams may require stronger attestation; mitigation: support cryptographic signing of manifests and exportable audit bundles.
Large backfills (terabytes) could cause operator throttling; mitigation: quota-aware backfill and chunked escrow with resume tokens.
